title: Proper base change on classical pro-étale complexes
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of
schemes, and let $g:Y'\to Y$ be arbitrary. Set $X'=X\times_YY'$, with
projections $f':X'\to Y'$ and $g':X'\to X$. If
$K\in D^+_{\mathrm{class}}(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ has torsion underlying
abelian cohomology sheaves, the canonical exchange, defined as in
[sk-def-exchange] from the pro-étale inverse and direct images $g^*,g'^*$ and
$Rf_*,Rf'_*$ on $D^+(\,\cdot_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$,

$$
g^*Rf_*K\longrightarrow Rf'_*g'^*K
$$

is an isomorphism in $D^+_{\mathrm{class}}(Y'_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$.

The complex $K$ need not be constructible, and the torsion orders need not be
invertible on $Y$. Classicality of $K$ is required: it is what brings the
statement back to the étale site.

proof.text: Write $A_T=\nu_T^*$. The comparison unit and classical equivalence give $L=R\nu_{X,*}K\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $\alpha:A_XL\cong K$. Exactness gives $A_XH^q(L)\cong H^q(K)$. Apply the torsion-reflection lemma to the exact fully faithful left adjoint $A_X$: every $H^q(L)$ has torsion underlying abelian sheaf.

source.place: Opening paragraph: classical descent and torsion reflection

proof.text: For a torsion abelian etale complex $E\in D^+$, choose a lower bound $a$ and put $\Phi=g^{-1}Rf_*$, $\Psi=Rf'_*g'^{-1}$. These are triangulated and their exchange commutes with shifts. Torsion assembly makes the exchange invertible at each $H^q(E)[0]$. Finite Postnikov propagation therefore makes it invertible at every $E_m=\tau_{\le m}E$ for $m\ge a-1$; for smaller $m$, $E_m=0$ by truncation cohomology and cohomology detection.

source.place: Bounded below complexes paragraph: finite induction

proof.text: Take $\mathcal P$ to be all primes; the torsion characterization puts $E$ in $D^+_{\mathcal P\text{-tor}}$. The truncation criterion gives isomorphisms $H^m\Phi(E_m)\cong H^m\Phi(E)$ and $H^m\Psi(E_m)\cong H^m\Psi(E)$. Naturality of the abelian exchange [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] identifies its bottom arrow with its invertible top arrow through these isomorphisms. Thus $H^m(\Ex_E)$ is invertible for every $m$, and cohomology detection makes $\Ex_E$ invertible.

source.place: Bounded below complexes paragraph: degreewise comparison, Stacks 05TC

proof.text: Forgetting coefficients sends $L$ to an abelian complex with the same underlying cohomology, so step 3 applies. The coefficient-forgetting comparison identifies the forgotten module exchange with that abelian exchange and reflects invertibility. Hence the specified etale module exchange $e_L$ is invertible.

The base change $f'$ is proper. Properness gives finite type and separatedness, hence $f,f'$ are qcqs. Apply the site comparisons to these direct-image edges and all inverse-image edges. Their unit/counit and composition coherence meets the hypotheses of the three-step adjunction-comparison lemma for the two unit--square--counit exchange formulas. It gives vertex isomorphisms $V_i$ with $V_iA_{Y'}(e_i)=p_iV_{i-1}$ for the three factors. Composing gives $V_3A_{Y'}(e_L)=\Ex^p_{A_XL}V_0$; thus $\Ex^p_{A_XL}$ is invertible.

source.place: Pro-etale paragraph: qcqs comparison and composition of the three mate squares

proof.text: Naturality along $\alpha:A_XL\cong K$ conjugates the preceding exchange to the one at $K$. Both endpoints are bounded below and classical: the site comparisons identify them with $A_{Y'}(g^{-1}Rf_*L)$ and $A_{Y'}(Rf'_*g'^{-1}L)$, which lie in the classical essential image by the derived equivalence. This full subcategory contains the inverse, proving the asserted isomorphism.

source.place: Pro-etale paragraph: naturality and bounded-below classical endpoints
